query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Pre-coating the tungsten phase with a thin nickel (Ni) interlayer will suppress phase separation and interfacial void formation in a W–Cu composite, thereby enhancing its thermal conductivity under high heat-flux and irradiation conditions typical of joints between W-based plasma‐facing components and Cu-based cooling systems.
generation.material_initial_state: A W–Cu composite featuring either discrete tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten ligaments embedded in a copper matrix that, in its untreated form, displays phase separation and void formation at the W–Cu interfaces under service conditions.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin Ni coating to the tungsten particles/ligaments (e.g., via physical vapor deposition or electroless plating) prior to composite consolidation.
generation.conditions: The Ni-coated tungsten is incorporated into the composite and consolidated (e.g., via spark plasma sintering or another suitable consolidation process) under processing conditions that mimic the service environment – including high heat flux and irradiation relevant to plasma-facing joint applications.
generation.structural_mediator: A modified W/Cu interfacial microstructure with improved wettability and bonding, resulting in reduced interfacial voids.
generation.mechanism: The Ni interlayer improves the wettability of tungsten with copper and promotes enhanced interdiffusion across the interface during consolidation, which helps prevent phase separation and the formation of voids under subsequent thermal and irradiation stresses.
generation.predicted_outcome: The primary measured property, thermal conductivity, is expected to increase relative to the untreated composite.
generation.baseline: The untreated W–Cu composite that exhibits phase separation and interfacial void formation under similar heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies to composites processed under conditions for plasma-facing applications where high heat flux, thermal cycling, and irradiation are encountered; processing parameters (like coating thickness and sintering temperature) are controlled variables not specified here.
generation.uncertainty: Although the qualitative improvement in thermal conductivity is anticipated, the precise magnitude of the enhancement is not quantified due to potential variability in coating uniformity, thickness, and processing parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of W–Cu composite samples under identical processing conditions; one set using tungsten particles with the Ni coating and one set without any coating. Subject both sets to accelerated heat-flux cycling and irradiation in a controlled environment that simulates service conditions.
measurements: High-resolution electron microscopy to quantify interfacial void fraction and assess phase separation at the W–Cu interfaces.
Thermal conductivity measurements (e.g., via Non-Equilibrium Molecular Dynamics simulations or experimental transient techniques) to compare the two sets.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Ni-coated samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in interfacial void formation and a corresponding increase in thermal conductivity compared to the untreated composite under identical high-heat and irradiation conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractIn this study, an effective way of applying Ti/Ni deposited coating to the surface of diamond single crystal particles by magnetron sputtering was proposed and novel high-entropy alloy (HEA)/diamond composites were prepared by spark plasma sintering (SPS). The results show that the interfacial bonding state of the coated diamond composite is obviously better than that of the uncoated diamond composite. Corresponding mechanical properties such as hardness, density, transverse fracture strength and friction properties of the coated diamond composite were also found to be better than those of the uncoated diamond composite. The effects of interface structure and defects on the mechanical properties of HEA/diamond composites were investigated. The research directions for further improving the structure and properties of high-entropy alloy/diamond composites were proposed. Keywords: high-entropy alloy, diamond, coating, interface, mechanical properties
